text.p: Dairy and food distribution company Unigate Plc is looking to expand its presence as a distributor in mainland Europe, said chairman Ian Martin.

"We have now refocused the group into food and distribution. And a lot of pan-European customers of ours are looking for us to come to them with some European capability, so one area we are looking at is distribution," he told a press conference.
Earlier the company reported net cash of 57.9 million at September 30, giving it ample resources for acquisitions.
Chief executive Ross Buckland told Reuters at the news conference Unigate had 200 to 300 million stg for acquisitions.
"If our interest cover went down below four times then you would have to question our cautiousness," he said.
He ruled out a special dividend, saying that growth by acquisition represented better value to shareholders.
"We are prepared to expand beyond areas in which we operate, into another food area, but if we did it would have to be a large and meaningful acquisition," said Buckland.
Martin told reporters, "We tend to see the duck being thickest in Europe and that is where we are shooting at the moment."
Wincanton, Unigate's distribution business, gained new business with Argos, British Airways, The Greenalls Group and H.J. Heinz in the six months to September 30.
Unigate completed its exit from the U.S. restaurant business with the sale of Taco Bueno and Casa Bonita for 27 million in August, enabling it to focus entirely on food and distribution in Europe.
Unigate also sold its minority stake in Dutch food company Nutricia for 360 million stg in January.Cash at the bank and in hand amounted to 292 million at the half-year stage.

The acquisition of French yoghurt and desert maker Prodigal and low-fat spread maker Vedial for 65 million stg in January 1995 was "illustrative of our ambitions to become more European" finance director John Worby told the news conference.
